rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questions raised about the distribution show that faith had not yet taken root fully in the objectors’ hearts.
rows.anchor: It is evident from such questions that faith had not fully found its roots in their hearts.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the revelation what God sent down to His servant credits the success to God through His Messenger; no group should claim it as its own achievement, since God can send help whenever He wills.
rows.anchor: On the contrary, they are: “that We sent down to Our servant.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Badr scene exemplifies the divine planning mentioned in the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: This verse depicts an example of God’s planning that was referred to in the previous verse.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s guidance brought the Prophet and Quraysh to Badr at the same time: the Prophet had been shown the caravan and army in a dream, then arrived as Quraysh came under the pretext of protecting the caravan.
rows.anchor: valley of Badr right at the time when on the opposite side the army of the Quraysh

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Timely arrival can determine a battle: delay risks defeat, arriving early brings danger, and Muslim supply problems made timing especially sensitive.
rows.anchor: Even a slight delay, at times can result in defeat.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God protected the Muslims from military stratagems; an army’s declaration or ultimatum may conceal its true target, and prior coordination would not readily have produced this meeting.
rows.anchor: The planning behind the declaration of war and giving ultimatum to the enemy

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s special planning made the believers meet their enemy so that the destined event would take place.
rows.anchor: God through His special planning made the believers face their enemy

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s death and life refer to spiritual death and life: the decisive encounter brings people to belief or disbelief with the proof made manifest.
rows.anchor: Death and life are referred to here in the spiritual sense.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabic preposition bi can mark the source or origin of something.
rows.anchor: delineating the source and origin of something.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Badr became a decisive proof between believers and disbelievers: the disbelievers had no excuse and the believers no ambiguity, with each side’s reality plain.
rows.anchor: The battle of Badr had become such a decisive event

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s hearing and knowledge encompass the entire unlikely arrangement, including hidden plans and inward whispers, by which He brought each party to the place for His intended result.
rows.anchor: He made each of them reach the right place

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God showed the believers the Quraysh as few and promised their defeat so weaker Muslims would keep their courage and avoid dispute over whether to fight; God knew their hearts’ weakness.
rows.anchor: God did this because if He had shown the

rows.speaker: some people
rows.claim: Some infer that prophets may be shown dreams contrary to reality because the Quraysh army was numerically large but appeared small in the Prophet’s dream.
rows.anchor: From this verse, some people have derived the result

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophetic dreams are revelation and cannot contradict reality; an apparently discrepant dream calls for interpretation.
rows.anchor: Dreams are among a means of revelation and hence the dream of a prophet can never

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi explains the apparent discrepancy symbolically: Quraysh was numerous in number but diminished in moral standing, and even a prophet may need to interpret a dream’s symbolism.
rows.anchor: a reality is shown in a symbolic way

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dream’s symbolic smallness reflects the Quraysh army’s weak moral standing, despite its large numerical size.
rows.anchor: Though the army of the disbelievers was large in number

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word qalīl can mean not only numerically few but also metaphorically or symbolically small.
rows.anchor: This is because this word does not only mean something

rows.speaker: Mu‘āwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān
rows.claim: Mu‘āwiyah’s cited verse uses smallness for low standing in an enemy’s eyes, contrasted with high standing among decent people.
rows.anchor: Thus, for example, Mu‘āwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān says:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general warning about losing courage and quarrelling targets the hesitant group described in 8:7, which wanted the caravan despite knowing the Prophet was going to face Quraysh and remained frightened after receiving glad tidings.
rows.anchor: This verse is actually directed to this group.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is addressed because he alone saw the dream; as the believers’ eye, what he sees concerns them all, so the response includes the whole community.
rows.anchor: A messenger of God is like the eye of the believers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse gives another example of divine help: God made both armies appear small to one another at first so they would not shrink from the destined decisive clash between truth and evil.
rows.anchor: This verse mentions another instance of help for the believers. The numbers were shown less to one another in the earlier stage

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers saw the believers’ actual small number but missed their moral strength; once that strength appeared in battle, the small Muslim force looked like a raging storm.
rows.anchor: They could not gauge its moral might which had practically transformed it into something formidable.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers saw Quraysh as few because God disclosed its moral weakness; the heart shapes sight, making obstacles small to the resolute and harmless things terrifying to the faint-hearted.
rows.anchor: One’s sight is subservient to one’s heart to a large extent.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A believer’s inner faith can make one person as strong as a thousand disbelievers; human strength and weakness arise from the inner self, a reality people can experience through faith.
rows.anchor: there was a time when a single believer had the same might as one thousand disbelievers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All outcomes come from God, including apparent changes in numbers, victory, and defeat; people should fulfill their duties and leave the outcome to Him.
rows.anchor: everything happens from God. Matters like the number of some group being shown less than its actual count or vice versa, granting victory or inflicting defeat – all comes from God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following verses turn from the Badr example to guidance for believers in future battles.
rows.anchor: These verses give direction to the believers for future stages.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Steadfastness requires believers to do their duty through available means before God’s help comes; they cannot sit still and demand victory as Israelites did.
rows.anchor: It is only when they do their due that the help of God comes to their rescue.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abundant remembrance sustains steadfastness by keeping faith alive; it is essential as air, since believers are always in conflict with Satan and need it especially in trials.
rows.anchor: This remembrance is as essential as air is essential for life.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Success includes this life and the next: dominance alone may occur without remembrance, but true success is God aided dominance lived in His company.
rows.anchor: “Success” is a comprehensive Word. This comprises success both in this world and in the next.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembrance of God is the source of morale and resolve for an army fighting for His cause, and thus a basis for steadfastness.
rows.anchor: Islam has said that it is God’s remembrance that boosts the morale of an army waging war for His cause.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obedience to God and His Messenger also calls for complete wartime discipline and immediate compliance with both divine and prophetic directives.
rows.anchor: believers must display immaculate discipline against

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning against disagreement states negatively the preceding call to steadfastness; division weakens morale and resolve.
rows.anchor: The words “and do not differ with one another

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A group of believers failed to follow this directive at Uhud, and the whole army suffered the consequences; 3:152 recounts their weakness, disagreement, and disobedience.
rows.anchor: this directive which was not followed by a group of believers

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commands fa-thbutū and wa-ṣbirū both mean remain steadfast; Islahi distinguishes the former as addressing individuals and the latter as addressing the group collectively.
rows.anchor: the latter word was said with respect to individuals

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Collective steadfastness makes a group worthy of divine help: God aids united, organized fighters, not a scattered and undisciplined force.
rows.anchor: He only helps those who fight for his cause
